chapter: Memphis boyhood and the Ohio territory years
title: Orphaned in Memphis and raised by illiterate grandparents
summary: Crawford recalls starting in high school in Memphis, losing his parents young and being raised by his grandparents, his grandmother a famed midwife.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Well, Stanley, I started out in Memphis, Tennessee, in high school under Jimmy Lansford's band, and I'm going back around about '28 and '29 now, and so we formed a little amateur high school orchestra, and so -- well, I just knew I was going (Inaudible), my mother, dad died when I was six, five or six. I was raised by my grandparents, who could neither read nor write. And she was the greatest midwife in the city of Memphis. She assisted in delivering more babies than any doctor in Memphis, white or colored, and also I mean Black or white babies. She didn't just deliver Blacks only or Negroes, I prefer to say, or colored.

Now, this woman was an amazing lady, without any formal education whatsoever, because she couldn't write, read nor write. My grandfather was the same a saint. They were the only parents I had besides an aunt, who's dead now, who lived across the street, and one of my grandfather's (inaudible).
